title: Kim Agent IPC Events
description: All typed events emitted from Python orchestrator → Rust subprocess.rs → Tauri → React. Edit this file and run 'npm run gen:events' to regenerate the TypeScript, Rust, and Python bindings.

events.description: A human-readable status message from the agent loop (activity feed item).

message.description: Status text to display in activity feed.

events.description: Agent emitted a structured plan with step list.
Agent advanced to a new plan step.
Agent completed a plan step.
Context window usage snapshot.

cumulative_input.description: Total input tokens consumed so far.

phase.description: Budget phase label (ok / warn / critical / full).

last_input.description: Input tokens in the last provider call.

last_output.description: Output tokens in the last provider call.

source.description: Provider identifier that produced this snapshot.

estimate.description: True when token count is estimated rather than exact.

events.description: Cumulative token usage for this run.
Window/UI control signal from the agent.

action.description: 'screenshot_flash' triggers flash overlay; 'show' brings main window to front.

events.description: Run completed (success or expected failure).

termination.description: Termination reason key: task_complete | max_iterations | stuck | provider_failed | need_help | cancelled | conversational_loop.

events.description: Run ended due to a recoverable or unrecoverable error.

recoverable.description: True when the user can retry without config changes.

events.description: Provider call failed with a specific error code.

code.description: Error code: auth | rate_limit | server_error | timeout | network | invalid_request.

retryable.description: True when automatic retry is possible.

events.description: Provider rate-limited; agent will retry after a delay.
Agent is requesting human approval before executing a high-risk tool.

risk.description: Risk level: high | medium. Determines UI prominence.

preview.description: K6: human-readable preview — command string, unified diff (<=40 lines), or URL + element label. May be empty.

id.description: T1 decision id — unique per approval request. Echo it back in the hitl_approve stdin line; a decision whose id does not match the currently pending request is discarded. May be empty on legacy emitters.

events.description: Human approval decision sent back to the agent.

tool.description: MCP tool name that was approved or denied.

approved.description: True if the user approved the tool call.

events.description: A tool invocation shown in the live activity feed.

args.description: Tool arguments used to build the activity label.

events.description: A final assistant answer to append to the conversation.

text.description: Answer text without a legacy marker prefix.

events.description: Line-count summary for a file changed by a tool.
A structured status, success, or error activity item.
Codex app-server: native per-command approval request. Block until the user answers with an approval_decision stdin line (accept | acceptForSession | decline).

id.description: Approval request id — echo it back in the approval_decision stdin line.

command.description: Full shell command codex wants to run.

cwd.description: Working directory the command would run in.

risk.description: Risk hint: 'network' when the command needs network access, else '' (sandbox escalation).

network.description: True when this is a managed-network approval (command needs network access).

amendment.description: Proposed execpolicy amendment tokens (allow similar commands without prompting); may be empty.

events.description: Codex app-server: native file-change (patch) approval request.

id.description: Approval request id — echo it back in the approval_decision stdin line.

files.description: Changed files: [{path, kind}] best-effort; may be empty.

events.description: Codex app-server: codex is asking the USER a question (item/tool/requestUserInput) or an MCP server raised an elicitation. Render the questions and answer via the respond_user_input Tauri command, which writes a {"type":"user_input","id":…,"answers":…} stdin line back to the bridge.

id.description: Request id — echo it back in the user_input stdin line (respond_user_input's id argument).

kind.description: 'questions' (codex requestUserInput) or 'elicitation' (MCP elicitation; informational — Kim auto-declines these today).

item_id.description: Codex thread item id the questions belong to; may be empty (always empty for elicitation).

questions.description: Question objects as sent by codex: [{id, header, question, options?: [{label, description?}], isOther?, isSecret?}]. Empty for elicitation.

message.description: Elicitation message text; empty for kind='questions'.

events.description: Codex app-server: live output chunk from a running command.

item_id.description: Command-execution item id this chunk belongs to.

chunk.description: Raw output chunk (may contain partial lines).

events.description: Codex app-server: streaming assistant-message text delta.
Codex app-server: streaming reasoning text delta (provider names scrubbed).
Codex app-server: the turn's plan checklist changed.

steps.description: Plan steps: [{text/step, status}] as sent by codex.

events.description: Codex app-server: cumulative unified diff of the turn's file changes.

unified_diff.description: Unified diff text (whole-turn snapshot, not incremental).

events.description: Codex app-server: codex-side transcript token usage snapshot.
Codex app-server: a thread item started or completed.

phase.description: 'started' or 'completed' (JSON-RPC method name, not the item's own outcome).

title.description: Human-readable label (command string, file list, …); may be empty.

status.description: The item's own outcome, distinct from `phase`. For commandExecution: 'inProgress' | 'completed' | 'failed' | 'declined'. Empty for kinds that carry no such status (agentMessage, reasoning, …) or on legacy emitters.

events.description: Codex app-server: a turn started / completed / was interrupted.
Agent completed its execution successfully or with expected outcome.

success.description: True when the agent finished successfully.

events.description: Agent execution was cancelled.
Agent run failed with an error.
